5 files, ~120 lines total. No `package.json`, no tests, no README — this is the entire repo as it stands.

**The flow: `server.js` → `auth.js` → `routes.js` → `cache.js` → `store.js`**

## 1. `server.js` — entry point
Raw Node `http` server (no framework). Every request: verify the `Authorization` header via `auth.js`, reject with 401 if invalid, otherwise hand off to `route()`. Listens on `PORT` env var or 8080.

## 2. `auth.js` — bearer tokens
Custom scheme, not JWT: token is `<userId>.<hexSignature>`, where signature is `HMAC-SHA256(userId, SECRET)`. Verifies with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` (good — avoids timing attacks). `SECRET` defaults to `'dev-secret'` if `AUTH_SECRET` isn't set in env — fine for dev, a real gap if that default ever ships to prod.

## 3. `routes.js` — the route table
A plain object mapping `"METHOD /path"` → handler function:
- `GET /users` → `cached()` wrapping `getUser`
- `GET /orders` → `cached()` wrapping `listOrders`
- `POST /orders` → `putOrder` directly (bypasses cache)

Unmatched routes get 404, handler errors get 500 with `err.message` (worth noting: that leaks internal error text to clients).

## 4. `cache.js` — read-through LRU
256-entry in-memory LRU sitting in front of the store. No TTL of its own — relies on the store to own freshness.

## 5. `store.js` — the "database"
It's an in-memory `Map`, not a real DB. Every record TTLs out 15 minutes after last write.

## Heads-up: cache/write inconsistency
`routes.js` comment claims writes "invalidate the affected keys" — they don't. `POST /orders` calls `putOrder()` in `store.js`, which never touches the `cache.js` LRU. So after a write, `GET /orders` can keep serving a stale cached list until that cache entry ages out on its own (LRU eviction only, no TTL). Worth fixing if this is more than a toy — want me to add the invalidation call?

**Next:** run `Get-ChildItem -Force` one level up from here to confirm there really is no `package.json`/git history hiding elsewhere — if this truly is the whole repo, there's no way to run or test it yet.
